newsitem.title: UK: BMA/BA to discuss interline cargo agreement.
newsitem.headline: BMA/BA to discuss interline cargo agreement.

text.p: British Mediterranean Airways (BMA) and British Airways Plc are to hold talks in the next few weeks on a possible cargo interline agreement, BMA managing director Des Hetherington said.

Last week, BMA and BA agreed on a passenger franchise pact covering some UK-Middle East routes, effective March 30. In October, they decided not to proceed with a franchise agreement when BMA had been unable to meet its conditions.

"Cargo is treated as a totally separate matter" by both BA and BMA and "the agreement we have with our UK cargo general sales agent Commercial Transport International (CTI) has worked very well and we want it to continue," Hetherington told Reuters.

"But at the same time we would like to bring in the strengths of BA's international network and get it to feed our services with cargo. This is where the proposed interlining agreement comes in," he said.
Hetherington is planning to discuss this with BA World Cargo's network strategy manager Gerry Devine.

BMA reckons cargo earnings could rise to nearly 10 percent of total earnings on its planned new UK-Georgia route compared to under five percent now on its existing services from London Heathrow to Beirut, Damascus and Amman.
Flying as a franchise carrier in BA livery, BMA will be the sole operator on these routes as BA is dropping services it previously duplicated with BMA from March 30 owing to a lack of profitability.
BMA plans to start three new weekly franchised services from Heathrow to Tbilisi, Georgia, and three a week to Alexandria in Egypt, all with Airbus A320 aircraft, on April 14.
As part of the agreement, BMA will increase its current five flights a week to Beirut to a daily service, its Amman services to five from three a week and to Damascus to four from two.
BMA is to lease two further A320s, which can carry up to 3.5 tonnes of cargo, from Airbus Industrie to add to the A320 leased from Dublin-based Orix Aviation.

"We attract only limited cargo flows to Amman, Beirut and Damascus and this represents less than five percent of our total revenues," noted Hetherington who hopes the London-Beirut flights would be increased to a daily frequency later this year while Amman "has the potential to go daily within 12 months".
BMA is looking for further route expansion "to points in the Levant and Near East region, and to former CIS states", Hetherington said but declined to elaborate.
